content: Ligand 1 is my best molecule, ligand 2 is its 5-methyl isomer at 0.14 - a useful reminder that this pharmacophore is exquisitely position-sensitive even though it is substituent-insensitive at C4. Methyl 0.41, cyclopropyl 0.43 and methoxy 0.42 at C4 are all equivalent, which rules out a simple electronic story, but every one of those groups is electron-releasing. A chlorine is the missing case: comparable in size to a methyl, but strongly electron-withdrawing and a pi-acceptor rather than a donor. If C4 really only cares about occupying a compact pocket, chlorine should land near 0.41; if it drops, the group's electronics matter after all and I have been reading the structure-activity wrong. Atom 14 is the cap cyclopropane CH bonded to the carbonyl at atom 12 over a non-ring bond, so anchoring there keeps the cyclopropane and I rebuild everything else, holding the cap constant so the only variable is the C4 substituent. Expected product: N-{4-[(4-chloropyridin-2-yl)amino]phenyl}cyclopropanecarboxamide at about 288 Da.
